title: Maths reference: Linear relations
summary: The words and methods from Linear relations, each with an example and, where it helps, a picture of the board.
_about: Maths cards for maths/linear-relations (see snippets/maths.json for the format).

items.label: growing pattern
items.hint: What each new figure adds goes in front of $n$; what is there at the start goes on its own. Figure 4 has $3 \times 4 + 1 = 13$ sticks.
items.board:
widget: pattern
shape: squares
n: 1, 8, 4
count: on
items.shows: Figure 4: each square adds 3 sticks, plus 1 at the start

items.label: rule
items.hint: A rule turns each input $x$ into an output $y$. Put the input in for $x$: $x = 3$ gives $y = 2 \times 3 + 1 = 7$.

items.label: table of values
items.hint: Choose inputs, work out each output from the rule ($y = 2x + 1$ here), and write them in pairs.

items.label: ordered pair
items.hint: Input first, then output. To plot it: across 2 on the $x$-axis, then up 5.
items.board:
widget: graph
x: -1, 5
y: -1, 8
point A: 2, 5

items.label: reading a graph
items.hint: Find the value you know on its axis, go to the line, then read across to the other axis. Sections of a graph increase, decrease or stay constant.

items.label: vary one variable
items.code: V = l \times w \times h \quad (\text{change } h \text{ only})
items.hint: To see what one letter does, change only that letter and keep the others the same. Record the results in a table.

items.label: gradient
items.hint: $m$, the number in front of $x$: one step right, the line goes up $m$ (down when $m$ is negative). A bigger $m$ is steeper; $m = 0$ is flat.
items.board:
widget: graph
x: -1, 5
y: -2, 14
plot: y = 3x + 1
step: 1

items.label: y-intercept
items.hint: $c$, the number on its own: where the line crosses the $y$-axis (at $x = 0$). Changing $c$ moves the line up or down without changing its steepness.

items.label: parallel lines
items.hint: The same $m$ gives the same steepness, so the lines never meet. $y = 2x + 4$ is $y = 2x + 1$ moved up 3.
items.board:
widget: graph
x: -1, 5
y: -1, 14
plot: y = 2x + 1
plot: y = 2x + 4
items.shows: y = 2x + 1 and y = 2x + 4: same m, so parallel

items.label: vertical and horizontal lines
items.hint: One letter: every point on $x = 3$ has $x = 3$ (a vertical line); every point on $y = -2$ has $y = -2$ (horizontal).

items.label: inequality region
items.hint: Draw the boundary $y = 2x + 1$: dashed for $<$ and $>$, solid for $\le$ and $\ge$. Test a point such as $(0, 0)$: true, shade its side; false, the other side.
items.board:
widget: graph
x: -4, 5
y: -5, 8
shade: y < 2x + 1
point O: 0, 0
items.shows: y < 2x + 1: below the dashed line, including (0, 0)

items.label: solve with a graph
items.hint: Draw each side as a line: $y = 2x + 3$ and $y = 11$. Where they meet, both sides are equal, so the $x$ there is the solution.
items.board:
widget: graph
x: -1, 7
y: -1, 16
plot: y = 2x + 3
plot: y = 11
cross: 1, 2

items.label: rule from a situation
items.hint: A starting amount plus a rate: the start is $c$ (4 dollars to get in) and the rate is $m$ (2 dollars per km).

items.label: comparing two plans
items.hint: Put both rules on one graph. Where the lines cross, the plans cost the same; on either side, the lower line is cheaper. Check where the model makes sense (no negative gigabytes).
